label: LTX 2.3 — Image-to-Video mit Audio & Dialog

must: Everything goes into main_prompt as one continuous block: the action, the camera path, the sound and any dialogue. There are no separate motion, audio or camera fields - the user pastes main_prompt into a single field in the generator.
Plain English prose. No headings, no labels, no bullet lists.
Open with the state of the opening frame, untimed, only as far as needed to anchor who is where.
Then drive the action with time brackets in the form [0-4 sec], [4-6 sec], [6-11 sec], [11+ sec]. The last bracket is open-ended. Brackets run in order and must not overlap.
Inside each bracket describe every moving body part, every composition change and every manipulation in that window - plus the reaction it causes.
If the scene is explicit, use full anatomical terminology and visually representable erotic detail.
Put sound where it happens: ambience, foley, natural and explicit sounds, either inside the bracket they belong to or as one closing sentence describing the whole soundscape.
Dialogue goes in quotation marks, preceded by the voice tone, inside the bracket where it is spoken. Keep lines short - long dialogue costs video quality.
avoid: A bracket that describes no change - if nothing happens, merge it with the previous one.
Embellishment that describes nothing visible or audible.
Long rambling dialogue - it degrades video quality.
Background music description unless no dialogue and no soundscape fits the scene.

notes_for_model: LTX 2.3 consumes one long plain-text block and generates synchronised audio. Time brackets like [0-4 sec] are the working format on this setup - they anchor motion, sound and dialogue to the same timeline. The negative prompt here mostly suppresses unwanted AUDIO (music, narration, bleeps, foreign language) alongside the usual visual artefacts.
